sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于对设计的热爱以及围绕设计的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, how is it possible that three months after admitting defeat, the Republicans are back with yet another plan to repeal the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 今天，为什么在承认失败三个月后，共和党人竟然又带着另一项废除《平价医疗法案》的计划卷土重来了？

sentences.en: And after sinking the last plan, will John McCain do it again, but this time by voting against his best friend in the Senate?
sentences.zh: 在否决了上一个计划后，约翰·麦凯恩会再次出手吗？但这次他要投票反对他在参议院最好的朋友？

sentences.en: It's Thursday, September 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月21日，星期四。

sentences.en: I'm here.
sentences.zh: 我在这儿。

sentences.en: Can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 你能听到我吗？

sentences.en: I can.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Am I connected?
sentences.zh: 我连上了吗？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: This is fancy, this whole setup.
sentences.zh: 这太高级了，整个设置。

sentences.en: This is so cool to have you.
sentences.zh: 能请到你真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Last time we talked to you was via cell phone at like two in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我们上次和你通话还是在凌晨两点左右，通过手机。

sentences.en: It was in the middle of the night and I have basically no recollection of it.
sentences.zh: 那是半夜，我基本上没什么印象了。

sentences.en: I'm in the Senate press gallery, just where you want to be at 2.11 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我现在在参议院新闻发布厅，凌晨2点11分，这正是你该待的地方。

sentences.en: Tom, what just happened?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，刚才发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, in some ways it's as simple as the seven-year Republican quest to dismantle the Affordable Care Act collapsed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某种程度上，事情很简单，共和党人七年来试图拆解《平价医疗法案》的努力失败了。

sentences.en: This certainly seems like the end of the road for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这看起来确实像是共和党人的穷途末路。

sentences.en: So, Tom Kaplan, how is it possible that you are now back on the line with me and we are talking about another Republican attempt to repeal the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆·卡普兰，为什么你现在又连线我，我们还在谈论共和党人又一次试图废除《平价医疗法案》？

sentences.en: It actually goes back in July.
sentences.zh: 其实这要追溯到七月份。

sentences.en: With all of the controversy surrounding the Republican Obamacare replacement bill, one GOP senator is working on unveiling his own health care plan.
sentences.zh: 在围绕共和党奥巴马医改替代法案的争议中，一位共和党参议员正致力于推出他自己的医疗保健计划。

sentences.en: A couple of senators started working on their own kind of alternative proposal for repealing and replacing the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 几位参议员开始着手制定他们自己的替代方案，旨在废除并取代《平价医疗法案》。

sentences.en: And what we attempted to do, and we're going to introduce this as part of the Graham-Cassidy Amendment,
sentences.zh: 我们试图做的是——我们将把这作为“格雷厄姆-卡西迪修正案”的一部分引入，

sentences.en: in which we attempt to establish fairness for all Americans in terms of the support they receive from the federal taxpayer.
sentences.zh: 我们试图在所有美国人从联邦纳税人那里获得的支持方面建立公平性。

sentences.en: And this didn't get a ton of attention.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有引起太多的关注。

sentences.en: It was kind of seen as an idea that they had that probably wasn't going to go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 它被视为一个他们提出的、可能不会有什么结果的想法。

sentences.en: But they kept at it.
sentences.zh: 但他们坚持了下来。

sentences.en: They've worked on it over the past month or two and came out with a bill a week ago.
sentences.zh: 过去一两个月他们一直在为此努力，并在一周前拿出了法案。

sentences.en: And they've managed to actually get some momentum here and get other Republicans on board.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然真的在这里获得了一些动力，并让其他共和党人加入了进来。

sentences.en: Wouldn't you like to export natural gas to cut Putin's legs out from under him?
sentences.zh: 难道你不想出口天然气来拆普京的台吗？

sentences.en: So, Lindsey Graham from South Carolina is a colorful, wisecracking presence at the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 所以，来自南卡罗来纳州的林赛·格雷厄姆是国会山上一位色彩鲜明、妙语连珠的人物。

sentences.en: I'm not afraid of a guy riding around on a horse without his shirt.
sentences.zh: 我不怕一个光着膀子骑马的人。

sentences.en: The guy's got a pair of twos and we've got a full house and he's walking all over Obama.
sentences.zh: 那家伙手里只有一对二，而我们有满堂红，他却在奥巴马面前横行霸道。

sentences.en: John McCain's best friend in the Senate, not someone who is thought of as focused on health care.
sentences.zh: 他是约翰·麦凯恩在参议院最好的朋友，并不是那种被认为专注于医疗保健的人。

sentences.en: He's teamed up with Bill Cassidy from Louisiana, who is not super well-known.
sentences.zh: 他与来自路易斯安那州的、不太出名的比尔·卡西迪联手了。

sentences.en: He's a doctor and he's really into health care policy.
sentences.zh: 他是一名医生，而且非常热衷于医疗保健政策。

sentences.en: They have to take all the dollars that would go to a state and deliver it to the state.
sentences.zh: 他们必须把本应拨给各州的资金全部拿走，然后再分发给各州。

sentences.en: The state would have to use it on health care, but then allow that state to come up with a solution particular for their state.
sentences.zh: 各州必须将其用于医疗保健，但要允许该州提出适合其自身的解决方案。

sentences.en: And they've made kind of an interesting pairing to try to bring the repeal push back to life.
sentences.zh: 他们组成了一个有趣的搭档，试图让废除医改的努力起死回生。

sentences.en: So, let me understand this.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我理一理。

sentences.en: How do Republicans again get to this point where they're again talking about health care, though?
sentences.zh: 共和党人究竟是怎么走到这一步，再次谈论医疗保健的呢？

sentences.en: Because it just seemed so over.
sentences.zh: 因为这看起来已经彻底结束了。

sentences.en: It looked like September was going to be a nightmare of a month because Congress needed to pass a spending measure to keep the government open.
sentences.zh: 九月看起来将是一个噩梦般的月份，因为国会需要通过一项支出法案来维持政府运转。

sentences.en: And they also had to raise the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还必须提高债务上限。

sentences.en: And that looked like it was going to be this big, messy fight to everyone's surprise.
sentences.zh: 这看起来会是一场巨大的、混乱的斗争，出乎所有人的意料。

sentences.en: Great meeting with Chuck Schumer, Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 与查克·舒默、南希·佩洛西的会面很棒。

sentences.en: The president met with congressional leaders this morning where he broke with the GOP and sided with Democrats.
sentences.zh: 总统今天上午会见了国会领导人，他在会上与共和党决裂，站在了民主党一边。

sentences.en: In a stunning move, President Trump bucking his own party, cutting a deal with Democrats to provide disaster relief funding,
sentences.zh: 在一项令人震惊的举动中，特朗普总统违背了自己所在的党派，与民主党达成协议，提供救灾资金，

sentences.en: extend the debt ceiling and fund the government for three months.
sentences.zh: 延长债务上限，并为政府提供三个月的资金。

sentences.en: And that was a tough pill to swallow for Republicans who were completely blindsided.
sentences.zh: 这对完全被蒙在鼓里的共和党人来说，是一个难以接受的苦果。

sentences.en: But it sort of cleared the decks for the rest of September instead of having this big fiscal fight that was resolved much earlier than everyone thought it would be.
sentences.zh: 但这在某种程度上为九月份剩下的时间扫清了障碍，而不是进行这场比所有人预期更早解决的重大财政斗争。

sentences.en: So, in striking a deal with the Democrats on the budget, President Trump and the Democrats, Pelosi and Schumer, opened up another chance for Republicans to repeal Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 所以，在与民主党达成预算协议时，特朗普总统和民主党人佩洛西、舒默为共和党人废除奥巴马医改开启了另一个机会。

sentences.en: That's striking.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全是这样。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, it's a number of different factors people are talking about.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们谈论的是许多不同的因素。

sentences.en: Another thing that happened this month that kind of gets brought up by Republicans is Senator Bernie Sanders went public with his proposal for a Medicare for all system.
sentences.zh: 本月发生的另一件事被共和党人提了出来，那就是伯尼·桑德斯参议员公布了他的“全民医保”提案。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We spoke to him about it.
sentences.zh: 我们和他谈过这件事。

sentences.en: We are the only major country on earth not to guarantee health care to all people.
sentences.zh: 我们是地球上唯一没有保证全民医疗保健的主要国家。

sentences.en: And I think it's time that we end to that.
sentences.zh: 我认为是时候结束这种情况了。

sentences.en: And we do that most efficiently and easily by expanding Medicare to all.
sentences.zh: 我们通过将医保扩大到全民，可以最高效、最容易地做到这一点。

sentences.en: And it added sort of another issue that Republicans certainly latched onto once Senator Sanders went public with that push.
sentences.zh: 这增加了另一个问题，一旦桑德斯参议员公开了这一推动计划，共和党人肯定就抓住了这一点。

sentences.en: Is what you're kind of saying that Republicans don't like the taste of all this Democratic enthusiasm and activity in the air and that they're thinking to themselves,
sentences.zh: 你是不是在说，共和党人不喜欢空气中弥漫的这种民主党人的热情和活动，他们在想，

sentences.en: you know what, let's just try this one more time.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，让我们再试一次。

sentences.en: Because it looks like there's just a little too much momentum against the backs of the Democrats when it comes to this kind of an issue.
sentences.zh: 因为看起来在处理这类问题时，民主党背后的势头似乎太强了。

sentences.en: There definitely is a feeling among Republicans in Congress that they need to get a win.
sentences.zh: 国会的共和党人确实有一种需要赢得胜利的感觉。

sentences.en: The other factor is the calendar,
sentences.zh: 另一个因素是时间表，

sentences.en: which is Republicans only have till the end of this month in order to be able to pass a repeal bill and not run into a Democratic filibuster in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 共和党人只有到本月底才能通过废除法案，否则就会在参议院遭遇民主党的阻挠议事。

sentences.en: So this is kind of the last moment they could do it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们能做的最后时刻了。

sentences.en: Explain that deadline to me.
sentences.zh: 给我解释一下这个截止日期。

sentences.en: Why do we keep hearing about September 30th?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们一直听到9月30日这个日期？

sentences.en: So Republicans have 52 seats in the Senate and they are using special budget rules to try to pass their repeal bill with just a simple majority.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在参议院有52个席位，他们正在利用特殊的预算规则，试图以简单多数通过他们的废除法案。

sentences.en: Then in this case, the special rules they want to use to pass this with just 50 votes, they expire at the end of the fiscal year and the fiscal year ends at the end of September.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们想要用来以50票通过法案的特殊规则，在财政年度结束时就会失效，而财政年度在9月底结束。

sentences.en: So that's why we're talking about this as kind of the last moment where they could do it.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我们把它称为他们能做的最后时刻。

sentences.en: So we should think of September 30th as the last possible day that Republicans have the easiest possible path to passing something as complicated as repealing the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该把9月30日视为共和党人通过像废除《平价医疗法案》这样复杂的事情，所拥有的最后可能的机会。

sentences.en: That's the right way to look at it.
sentences.zh: 这是看待这个问题的正确方式。

sentences.en: So our last hope, we think, is relieving folks from the burdens of the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为，我们最后的希望是让人们从《平价医疗法案》的负担中解脱出来。

sentences.en: If we give the states the flexibility to come up with their own solutions, they will find solutions that work better for their state than the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 如果我们给各州灵活性来提出他们自己的解决方案，他们会找到比《平价医疗法案》更适合他们州的方案。

sentences.en: And it makes total sense.
sentences.zh: 这完全说得通。

sentences.en: Clearly, Alaska is different than Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 显然，阿拉斯加与罗德岛不同。

sentences.en: Louisiana is different than Missouri.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那与密苏里不同。

sentences.en: I recall that a major complaint about the Affordable Care Act is that it brings a kind of one-size-fits-all approach to health care to every state that expanded Medicaid,
sentences.zh: 我记得对《平价医疗法案》的一个主要抱怨是，它给每个扩大了医疗补助计划的州带来了一种“一刀切”的医疗保健方法，

sentences.en: which was allowable under the law.
sentences.zh: 这是法律所允许的。

sentences.en: Is this an attempt to kind of give states the freedom to do what they want to do with a certain amount of money or not do anything at all and therefore just kind of put health care back in the states and take it away from the federal government?
sentences.zh: 这是否是一种尝试，即给各州自由，让他们用一定数量的钱去做他们想做的事，或者什么都不做，从而把医疗保健权还给各州，从联邦政府手中收回？

sentences.en: That's the idea, and it's an idea that Republicans really like, the idea of federalism,
sentences.zh: 这就是这个想法，而且共和党人非常喜欢联邦主义这个理念，

sentences.en: that states can choose to put in place the policies that they think are best for their residents.
sentences.zh: 即各州可以选择实施他们认为最适合其居民的政策。

sentences.en: Is this a partisan approach to health care?
sentences.zh: 这是一种党派性的医疗保健方法吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: Let me tell you how this works.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你这是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: I like Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢马萨诸塞州。

sentences.en: I like Maryland.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢马里兰州。

sentences.en: I like New York.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢纽约州。

sentences.en: I like California.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: But I don't like them that much.
sentences.zh: 但我没那么喜欢它们。

sentences.en: It would repeal the mandates that most people have to have health coverage, that large employers offer health coverage.
sentences.zh: 它将废除大多数人必须拥有医疗保险的强制规定，以及大型雇主必须提供医疗保险的规定。

sentences.en: It would repeal the expansion of Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 它将废除医疗补助计划的扩张。

sentences.en: It would repeal the tax credits that are provided to help people buy insurance on the individual market.
sentences.zh: 它将废除为帮助人们在个人市场上购买保险而提供的税收抵免。

sentences.en: And it would also allow states to get waivers so that insurers could charge people more if they have preexisting conditions.
sentences.zh: 它还将允许各州获得豁免，以便保险公司在人们有既往病史的情况下可以收取更高的费用。

sentences.en: So some of those consumer protections under the Affordable Care Act could also be rolled back.
sentences.zh: 因此，《平价医疗法案》下的一些消费者保护措施也可能被撤销。

sentences.en: Tom, the last time we talked and the last time Republicans proposed repealing the Affordable Care Act, the fate of the bill came down to three or four senators,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们上次谈话时，以及共和党人上次提议废除《平价医疗法案》时，法案的命运取决于三四位参议员，

sentences.en: and we got to know all of their names.
sentences.zh: 我们记住了他们所有人的名字。

sentences.en: Are those the same senators that hold the fate of this bill, or are they different?
sentences.zh: 是同样的参议员掌握着这项法案的命运，还是换了人？

sentences.en: It's the same ones.
sentences.zh: 还是同一批人。

sentences.en: It's the sort of Groundhog Day phenomenon at the Capitol, where suddenly we're chasing the same senators around, asking them where they stand,
sentences.zh: 这就像国会山上的“土拨鼠日”现象，我们突然又在追着同样的参议员，问他们的立场，

sentences.en: just as we were a couple of months ago.
sentences.zh: 就像几个月前一样。

sentences.en: Kentucky Senator Rand Paul is walking away from this current proposal, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 肯塔基州参议员兰德·保罗至少目前正在远离这个提案。

sentences.en: And he could be the one vote standing in the way of Obamacare repeal if it goes down that way.
sentences.zh: 如果事情真的那样发展，他可能会成为阻碍奥巴马医改废除的一票。

sentences.en: Republicans were only one vote shy last time around.
sentences.zh: 上次共和党人只差一票。

sentences.en: Where did the vote stand on this new effort, Graham-Cassidy?
sentences.zh: 这次“格雷厄姆-卡西迪”的新努力投票情况如何？

sentences.en: You're looking at people like Senator Lisa Murkowski, who voted against this.
sentences.zh: 你看看像丽莎·穆尔科斯基参议员这样的人，她上次投了反对票。

sentences.en: She says she's undecided.
sentences.zh: 她说她还没决定。

sentences.en: Susan Collins, still looking at this as well.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·柯林斯也还在观望。

sentences.en: And, of course, John McCain, the individual who effectively sunk this plan in July with the thumbs down.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有约翰·麦凯恩，那个在七月份用大拇指向下有效地否决了这个计划的人。

sentences.en: There certainly is some suspicion that Senator McCain this time could vote for it.
sentences.zh: 确实有人怀疑麦凯恩参议员这次可能会投赞成票。

sentences.en: Having said that, McCain hates the process.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，麦凯恩讨厌这个过程。

sentences.en: This is his big complaint, is the Senate is not following what is called regular order.
sentences.zh: 这是他最大的抱怨，即参议院没有遵循所谓的“常规程序”。

sentences.en: He wants committee hearings.
sentences.zh: 他想要委员会听证会。

sentences.en: He wants debate.
sentences.zh: 他想要辩论。

sentences.en: He wants amendments.
sentences.zh: 他想要修正案。

sentences.en: He wants sort of a much more deliberative process.
sentences.zh: 他想要一个更加审慎的过程。

sentences.en: And he's unapologetic about wanting this.
sentences.zh: 而且他对自己想要这些并不感到抱歉。

sentences.en: And then that leaves Murkowski from Alaska.
sentences.zh: 然后就剩下阿拉斯加的穆尔科斯基了。

sentences.en: From Alaska.
sentences.zh: 来自阿拉斯加。

sentences.en: And she is hard to read.
sentences.zh: 她很难读懂。

sentences.en: She has not said much this week.
sentences.zh: 她这周没说什么。

sentences.en: But a lot of attention in the coming days will be focused on Lisa Murkowski.
sentences.zh: 但未来几天，很多注意力将集中在丽莎·穆尔科斯基身上。

sentences.en: How does President Trump feel about this version of the repeal bill?
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统对这个版本的废除法案感觉如何？

sentences.en: We know that he has mercilessly lambasted Republican leadership for not getting this through last time.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他曾无情地抨击共和党领导层上次没能通过法案。

sentences.en: Called it embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 称其为令人尴尬。

sentences.en: So what about this bill?
sentences.zh: 那么这个法案呢？

sentences.en: He's on board.
sentences.zh: 他支持。

sentences.en: He took to Twitter.
sentences.zh: 他在推特上发声了。

sentences.en: Rand Paul is a friend of mine, but he is such a negative force when it comes to fixing health care.
sentences.zh: 兰德·保罗是我的朋友，但在修复医疗保健方面，他是一个消极的力量。

sentences.en: Graham-Cassidy bill is great.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆-卡西迪法案很棒。

sentences.en: And Obama cares.
sentences.zh: 而且奥巴马医改很糟糕。

sentences.en: And are there any real repercussions for Republicans if this goes to a vote and fails again, other than the presumed fury of President Trump?
sentences.zh: 如果这次投票再次失败，除了特朗普总统预想中的愤怒之外，对共和党人还有什么真正的后果吗？

sentences.en: There are a couple things.
sentences.zh: 有几件事。

sentences.en: I mean, there's the embarrassment factor of just going through this whole process again, having a vote, having a fail.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，再次经历整个过程、进行投票、再次失败，这本身就有尴尬的因素。

sentences.en: And it's like if you were embarrassed by not being able to fulfill your promise over the summer,
sentences.zh: 这就像如果你因为夏天没能兑现承诺而感到尴尬，

sentences.en: now you're just reminding people of your continued inability to fulfill that promise.
sentences.zh: 现在你只是在提醒人们你持续无法兑现承诺。

sentences.en: And there's certainly a question of, you know, Republicans are in control of the government.
sentences.zh: 当然还有一个问题，你知道，共和党人控制着政府。

sentences.en: At some point, do Americans start blaming Republicans for their insurance premiums going up and that kind of thing?
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，美国人会开始因为保险费上涨之类的事情而责怪共和党人吗？

sentences.en: So that's a question that will hang out there.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: But might it motivate President Trump to be even more likely to make deals with Democrats if he keeps finding that Republicans just can't get things like this done?
sentences.zh: 但如果特朗普总统发现共和党人总是无法完成这些事情，这会不会促使他更有可能与民主党人达成交易？

sentences.en: It's certainly in the realm of possibility that this fails again.
sentences.zh: 如果这次再次失败，这完全在可能性范围内。

sentences.en: He throws his hands up and decides that Chuck and Nancy, as he likes to say, are looking pretty good to him.
sentences.zh: 他可能会一摊手，决定正如他喜欢说的那样，查克和南希看起来对他来说还不错。

sentences.en: Now, having said that, tax reform is the next thing on the agenda.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，税制改革是议程上的下一项任务。

sentences.en: Tom, thank you.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: When we come back, how this bill is testing one of the most powerful friendships in Washington.
sentences.zh: 节目回来后，我们将探讨这项法案如何考验华盛顿最牢固的友谊之一。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上免费直播部分采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Cheryl Gastelberg, remind us who sunk health care in a way that we thought was for good back in July.
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔·加斯特尔伯格，提醒一下大家，七月份是谁以我们以为是彻底终结的方式否决了医疗改革？

sentences.en: Well, the man who sunk health care was John McCain, the senator from Arizona, very unpredictable senator.
sentences.zh: 嗯，否决医疗改革的人是来自亚利桑那州的参议员约翰·麦凯恩，他是一位非常难以预测的参议员。

sentences.en: It was an incredible, dramatic moment on Capitol Hill, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，那是在国会山上一个令人难以置信的戏剧性时刻。

sentences.en: McCain had just been diagnosed with brain cancer, and he came back to the Senate to, you know, a round of sustained applause less than two weeks after brain surgery.
sentences.zh: 麦凯恩当时刚被诊断出患有脑癌，他在脑部手术不到两周后回到参议院，迎接他的是一阵持续的掌声。

sentences.en: And then with a thumbs down, he signifies that he's not going to vote in favor of this Obamacare repeal.
sentences.zh: 然后，他竖起大拇指向下，表示他不会投票支持废除奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: And that's the vote that kills the bill.
sentences.zh: 那一票终结了这项法案。

sentences.en: And I remember that moment because it was literally like a Roman Coliseum scene of he holds up his hand and then slowly drags his thumb down.
sentences.zh: 我记得那一刻，简直就像古罗马斗兽场的场景，他举起手，然后慢慢地将大拇指朝下。

sentences.en: And it's at that moment that the Democrats realize that the Affordable Care Act will not be repealed.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，民主党人意识到《平价医疗法案》不会被废除了。

sentences.en: In their minds, it's over.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，一切都结束了。

sentences.en: And in Republican minds, too.
sentences.zh: 在共和党人看来也是如此。

sentences.en: Republicans were saying, well, this is it.
sentences.zh: 共和党人当时说，好吧，就是这样了。

sentences.en: But as we've just discussed, McCain's close friend, Lindsey Graham, is now trying to do this again to repeal the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们刚才讨论的，麦凯恩的密友林赛·格雷厄姆现在正试图再次推动废除《平价医疗法案》。

sentences.en: How was Graham feeling about health care at the time back in July?
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆在七月份时对医疗改革是什么态度？

sentences.en: Here's the state of play.
sentences.zh: 目前的局势是这样的。

sentences.en: All three of us support the idea of continuing the process to get a good outcome for the American people when it comes to replacing Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 我们三个人都支持继续推进这一进程，以便在取代奥巴马医改的问题上为美国人民争取一个好的结果。

sentences.en: What happened was McCain, Graham, and another senator, Ron Johnson of Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是，麦凯恩、格雷厄姆和另一位威斯康星州参议员罗恩·约翰逊，

sentences.en: held a press conference complaining that that bill, the so-called skinny repeal, was not a good bill.
sentences.zh: 召开了一场新闻发布会，抱怨那项所谓的“瘦身版废除法案”不是一项好法案。

sentences.en: The skinny bill as policy is a disaster.
sentences.zh: 作为政策，这个瘦身版法案是一场灾难。

sentences.en: The skinny bill as a replacement for Obamacare is a fraud.
sentences.zh: 作为奥巴马医改的替代方案，这个瘦身版法案是一场骗局。

sentences.en: But then, just hours later, Graham and Johnson voted to advance the bill.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅几个小时后，格雷厄姆和约翰逊就投票推进了该法案。

sentences.en: So Graham voted in support of the same bill that McCain voted against decisively.
sentences.zh: 所以格雷厄姆投票支持了麦凯恩曾果断投下反对票的同一项法案。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Give us the story of this friendship between these two men, McCain and Graham.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲麦凯恩和格雷厄姆这两位男士之间的友谊故事吧。

sentences.en: So I think the story of the friendship goes back, really, to when Lindsey Graham joins the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我认为这段友谊的故事要追溯到林赛·格雷厄姆加入参议院的时候。

sentences.en: He comes over to the Senate from the House in 2003.
sentences.zh: 他是在2003年从众议院转到参议院的。

sentences.en: And when Graham comes in, he is sort of instantly attached at the hip to McCain.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆一进来，就几乎立刻成了麦凯恩的“跟屁虫”。

sentences.en: And my illegitimate son, Lindsey Graham, is exploring that option.
sentences.zh: 而我的私生子林赛·格雷厄姆正在探索那个选项。

sentences.en: They're taking the same positions on foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 他们在外交政策上采取了相同的立场。

sentences.en: Don't forget, this is a time of muscular American intervention overseas.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，那是一个美国在海外进行强力干预的时代。

sentences.en: We're going to war with Iraq.
sentences.zh: 我们要对伊拉克开战了。

sentences.en: The starting point to me is the use of weapons of mass destruction by Saddam Hussein.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，起点是萨达姆·侯赛因使用大规模杀伤性武器。

sentences.en: What kind of weapons are we talking about that he used?
sentences.zh: 我们所说的他使用了什么样的武器？

sentences.en: We're going to find out massive evidence of weapons of mass destruction.
sentences.zh: 我们将发现大规模杀伤性武器的大量证据。

sentences.en: And we're going to find incredible brutality.
sentences.zh: 我们将发现令人难以置信的暴行。

sentences.en: There are all these issues that draw them together.
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题将他们联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And they start traveling on what is known in Washington as CODELs, short for Congressional Delegation Trips.
sentences.zh: 他们开始参加华盛顿所说的“国会代表团出访”（CODELs）。

sentences.en: These are official visits to foreign countries.
sentences.zh: 这些是对外国的正式访问。

sentences.en: Official.
sentences.zh: 正式的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Joining us now from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在加入我们的是来自美国驻阿富汗喀布尔大使馆的共和党参议员约翰·麦凯恩和林赛·格雷厄姆。

sentences.en: Embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan, is Republican Senators John McCain and Lindsey Graham.
sentences.zh: 所以这段关系由来已久。

sentences.en: So there's a relationship that goes back.
sentences.zh: 关于格雷厄姆和麦凯恩，有一点需要知道，他们都是军人出身。

sentences.en: One thing to know about both Graham and McCain is they're both military men.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆曾在空军担任军法官。

sentences.en: And Graham served in the Air Force as a judge advocate general.
sentences.zh: 关于林赛·格雷厄姆，还有一点需要知道的是，他的父母在他年轻时就去世了。

sentences.en: And another thing to know about Lindsey Graham is that his parents died when he was young.
sentences.zh: 他几乎是独自一人抚养大了妹妹。

sentences.en: And he raised a sister pretty much on his own.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他比约翰·麦凯恩年轻约15岁，甚至可能更多。

sentences.en: And he is also, I think, about 15 years younger than John McCain, maybe even more.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得格雷厄姆在某种程度上很敬仰麦凯恩，也许不是像父亲那样，而是像大哥那样。

sentences.en: I always felt that Graham, in a way, looked up to McCain, maybe not as a father figure, maybe as a big brother figure.
sentences.zh: 当然，约翰·麦凯恩是一位伟大的战争英雄。

sentences.en: And, of course, John McCain is an enormous war hero.
sentences.zh: 他在越南作为战俘的服役经历极具传奇色彩。

sentences.en: Kind of his service in Vietnam as a POW is storied.
sentences.zh: 所以我好奇这是否是一种纽带。

sentences.en: So I wonder if that is a bond.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一种非常牢固的纽带。

sentences.en: I think that's a very strong bond.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 说格雷厄姆崇拜麦凯恩并不为过。

sentences.en: I don't think it's too far to go to say that Graham idolizes McCain.
sentences.zh: 他最近告诉我，他在政治上所做的任何重要事情，没有一件是离开麦凯恩完成的。

sentences.en: He told me recently that there was nothing he'd ever done of consequence politically that he had done without McCain.
sentences.zh: 约翰常说，他宁愿输掉一场竞选，也不愿输掉一场战争。

sentences.en: John often says he would rather lose a campaign than lose a war.
sentences.zh: 在2008年麦凯恩与巴拉克·奥巴马竞选总统期间，格雷厄姆确实一直站在麦凯恩身边。

sentences.en: Graham was really at McCain's side during the time that McCain was running for president against Barack Obama in 2008.
sentences.zh: 这是个好消息。

sentences.en: Here's the good news.
sentences.zh: 我们将赢得这场战争，约翰·麦凯恩将成为我们下一任美国总统。

sentences.en: We're going to win this war and John McCain will be our next president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 后来格雷厄姆自己在2016年也进行了一次短暂的总统竞选，麦凯恩支持了他。

sentences.en: And then Graham himself had a very short-lived run for the presidency in 2016, and McCain supported him.
sentences.zh: 我相信林赛·格雷厄姆。

sentences.en: I believe in Lindsey Graham.
sentences.zh: 我相信他有资格和能力应对当今世界面临的挑战。

sentences.en: I believe that he has the credentials and the ability to address the challenges that are facing the world today.
sentences.zh: 超过，你知道……

sentences.en: Over, you know...
sentences.zh: 其他所有人。

sentences.en: Everybody else.
sentences.zh: 数不胜数，对吧？

sentences.en: Countless, right?
sentences.zh: 我想还有16位候选人。

sentences.en: 16, I think, other candidates.
sentences.zh: 当我竞选总统时，你们大多数人都错过了。

sentences.en: When I ran for president, most of you missed it.
sentences.zh: 约翰一直支持我。

sentences.en: John was with me.
sentences.zh: 底线是……

sentences.en: The bottom line...
sentences.zh: 他们是非常非常亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: They are very, very close friends.
sentences.zh: 这是一段深厚而真实的友谊，以至于不久前在CNN的市政厅会议上，当被问及他们的友谊时。

sentences.en: This is a deep and real friendship, so much so that not long ago when they were asked about their friendship during a CNN town hall.
sentences.zh: 他对朋友很忠诚。

sentences.en: He is loyal to his friends.
sentences.zh: 他热爱他的国家。

sentences.en: He loves his country.
sentences.zh: 如果为了国家他必须站出来反对自己的党派，那就随它去吧。

sentences.en: And if he has to stand up to his party for his country, so be it.
sentences.zh: 他会为这个国家献出生命。

sentences.en: He would die for this country.
sentences.zh: 我爱他爱得要死。

sentences.en: I love him to death.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到麦凯恩低下头，擦去了眼角的一点泪水。

sentences.en: And you could see McCain putting his head down and wiping a little tear from his eye.
sentences.zh: 格雷厄姆也热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: And Graham also was tearing up.
sentences.zh: 所以这就带我们回到了现在，回到了这一刻，回到了这个冠有格雷厄姆名字的医疗法案上。

sentences.en: So that brings us to now, to this moment, and to this health care bill that has Graham's name on it.
sentences.zh: 我们对约翰·麦凯恩对这项法案的看法了解多少？

sentences.en: What do we know about how John McCain feels about this bill?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他对自己意图的表态一直有点闪烁其词。

sentences.en: Well, he's been a little bit coy about his intentions.
sentences.zh: 他一直说他对投票支持这项法案持开放态度。

sentences.en: He's been saying all along that he's open to voting for this bill.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 他说他想听听亚利桑那州州长对该法案的看法。

sentences.en: That he wanted to hear from Arizona's governor about how the governor felt.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州州长道格·杜西确实公开支持了这项法案。

sentences.en: Arizona's governor, Doug Ducey, did come out in support of this bill.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，麦凯恩仍然表示他不确定自己会怎么做。

sentences.en: And once he did, McCain was still saying that he wasn't sure what he was going to do.
sentences.zh: 州长公开表示支持，这显然产生了一些影响。

sentences.en: The governor came out in favor, which obviously has some impact.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我们也没有走正常的程序。

sentences.en: But the fact is, we have also not gone through the regular order.
sentences.zh: 我不想知道。

sentences.en: I don't want to know.
sentences.zh: 我想知道有哪些修正案在议程上。

sentences.en: I want to know what amendments are in order.
sentences.zh: 我想知道为什么过去九个月里我们没有拿出一个成果。

sentences.en: I want to know why it is that we haven't had a product in the last nine months.
sentences.zh: 我想知道很多事情。

sentences.en: I want to know a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔，听起来你描述的是麦凯恩对你说的话。

sentences.en: And, Cheryl, what you're describing is something that McCain said to you, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是对我说的，也是对其他询问的记者说的。

sentences.en: Well, he said it to me, and he said it to any other reporters who asked.
sentences.zh: 整个星期他都被记者追问这件事。

sentences.en: He was being dogged by reporters all week about this.
sentences.zh: 我想在他跟我谈话时，他已经受够了。

sentences.en: And he was, I think he just had had it by the time he talked to me.
sentences.zh: 参议员，你和格雷厄姆参议员谈过这件事吗？

sentences.en: Senator, have you talked to Senator Graham about this?
sentences.zh: 你和他关系非常密切。

sentences.en: You're very close with him.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 你和格雷厄姆参议员谈过吗？

sentences.en: Have you talked to Senator Graham?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 你告诉他什么了？

sentences.en: And what have you told him?
sentences.zh: 我告诉他什么了？

sentences.en: What have I told him?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他我……

sentences.en: I've told him I.
sentences.zh: 他问你什么了？

sentences.en: What does he ask you?
sentences.zh: 他在催促你投票吗？

sentences.en: Is he pressing you for your vote?
sentences.zh: 我们不会互相施压。

sentences.en: We don't press each other.
sentences.zh: 他已经明确表示了他认为通过什么很重要。

sentences.en: He's made it clear what he thinks is important to get paSt.
sentences.zh: 本周我也和格雷厄姆谈过，我说，你知道，你和麦凯恩参议员谈过这件事吗？

sentences.en: I talked to Graham also this week and said, you know, have you talked to Senator McCain about this?
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，麦凯恩参议员可以自己做决定。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, Senator McCain can make up his own mind.
sentences.zh: 但当然，麦凯恩的投票是，你知道，这项法案正悬于一线。

sentences.en: But of course, McCain's vote is, you know, this bill is hanging by a thread.
sentences.zh: 他们需要每一张能争取到的选票才能通过它。

sentences.en: They need every vote they can get to pass it.
sentences.zh: 如果麦凯恩投反对票，这真的可能是共和党废除奥巴马医改努力的终结，真正的终结。

sentences.en: And if McCain votes against it, this really could be the end, the true end of the Republican effort to repeal Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么核心问题似乎变成了：麦凯恩会再次违背他的党派，甚至违背他的挚友林赛·格雷厄姆吗？

sentences.en: Which is why it feels like the essential question becomes, will McCain go against not just his party once again, but also his dear friend, Lindsey Graham?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我完全不知道。

sentences.en: Michael, I have absolutely no idea.
sentences.zh: 但我怀疑他会把自己的决定保密到最后。

sentences.en: But I also suspect he'll keep whatever decision he makes close to the veSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就会像上次一样，在参议院大厅的最后一刻看到结果。

sentences.en: And then we'll just see it at the last minute on the Senate floor like we did.
sentences.zh: 我们将看看它是得到大拇指向上还是向下的评价。

sentences.en: We'll see if it gets a thumbs up or a thumbs down.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，谢丽尔。

sentences.en: Thank you, Cheryl.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》报道称，特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒已要求白宫提供与特朗普总统一些最具争议的行为相关的文件，

sentences.en: The Times reports that special counsel Robert Mueller has asked the White House for documents related to some of President Trump's most controversial actions,
sentences.zh: 包括解雇国家安全顾问迈克尔·弗林以及罢免联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米。

sentences.en: including the firing of his national security advisor, Michael Flynn, and his dismissal of FBI director James Comey.
sentences.zh: 这些请求揭示了穆勒调查的范围，并表明调查的某些方面正直接聚焦于总统在白宫的行为。

sentences.en: The requests reveal the scope of Mueller's investigation and suggest that aspects of it are focused squarely on the president's behavior in the White House.
sentences.zh: 周二袭击墨西哥的7.1级地震已造成至少230人死亡，

sentences.en: And the 7.1 magnitude earthquake that struck Mexico on Tuesday has killed at least 230 people,
sentences.zh: 其中包括30名在小学倒塌时被困在里面的学生。

sentences.en: including 30 students who were trapped inside their elementary school when it collapsed.
sentences.zh: 随着数千名政府工作人员和志愿者开始救援工作，

sentences.en: The death toll is expected to rise significantly as thousands of government workers and volunteers begin recovery efforts,
sentences.zh: 在办公楼和公寓大楼的废墟中挖掘，预计死亡人数将大幅上升。

sentences.en: digging through the rubble of office buildings and apartment complexes.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《Metro》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
